mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening consumer demand and economic activity, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in improved economic prospects.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods when HOUST shows a rising trend over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 3.5% signals aggressive monetary easing by the central bank in response to economic weakness, which increases liquidity and risk appetite, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increases in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate a tightening labor market and strong job growth, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-shock recovery phase, a retail sales growth (RSAFS) above its 3-month moving average signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy rebounds.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods when RSAFS is above its 3-month moving average during the post-shock recovery regime.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI increase exceeding 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting expectations of monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) consistently signals a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days across most economic regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods when UNRATE is declining.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a broad-based economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as recession risks rise and corporate earnings expectations fall.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when INDPRO and HOUST both decline.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 2.0% signals robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in sustained corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods when GDPC1 exceeds 2.0%.
